correctness.rationale: For all rank permutations with n>=2, threshold decomposition yields the exact weighted path-square energy. All three finite-state potential arrays satisfy 24 transition and 12 terminal inequalities in exact rational arithmetic; telescoping proves each global bound. Ceiling and summation give the finite integer guarantee. The exact integral of the upper envelope f is 13/24, giving the claimed asymptotic guaranteed endpoint. The package checker also tests 409112 finite rank configurations and 131053 subset states. Sharpness is explicitly unproved.

originality.rationale: The exact Lin–Han rank statistic has a published lower range guarantee -1/2+O(M/n), while this proof supplies a new uniform finite-sample integer support bound at M=2 with asymptotic guarantee -3/8. It is not a reparameterization of that earlier inequality. The available closely relevant primary text and public mathematical matches inspected do not establish the stronger implication. The equivalence risk from path-square extremal graph literature is disclosed; no independent historical priority is asserted.
residual_risks: A graph-arrangement or one-dimensional finite-range spin-energy theorem may imply one or more supporting inequalities under different terminology.
Accessible journal-version passages were not supplemented by a fully navigable publisher copy; full-text equivalence risk is limited but not disproved.
The stronger bound is not claimed sharp: incompatibility among nested threshold minimizers may prevent attainment.
Historical priority has not received independent verification.

value.rationale: A published multi-neighbour correlation coefficient needs interpretable finite-sample range guarantees. The exact-sample integer lower support bound strengthens the previously available fixed-M=2 -1/2+O(1/n) guarantee to an asymptotic -3/8 threshold, eliminating a fixed nontrivial interval of impossible values. The structural path-square and finite-state method explains the improvement, rather than relying on numerical optimization. Full attainability remains outside scope.
